analysis.title: GS - Wojdyla - AIS Positioning Reset - 20 Oct 2026
key_insights: Earnings season is picking up and will be closely watched given the AI unwind. 14% of the S&P reports this week and 44% next week.
Positioning is low and was reset lower after last week's moves, particularly in popular areas such as semis. The GS sentiment indicator has been negative for six straight weeks.
Wednesday marked the second-largest net selling in a year in the Global AI basket (GSXGGLAI).

US L/S net leverage fell 3.2 pts, the largest weekly decline since the week of Liberation Day. Global Information Technology was the most net sold sector, with the largest net selling on GS PB records.
Essentially all of the fall in hedge fund net exposure since the end of July came from an increase in shorts, not a reduction in longs.
The next market move depends largely on earnings confirmation. Focus prints this week are SPCX (10/20) and META and TSLA (10/21).

Into META (reports 10/21 after the close), the buyside is braced for a top-line beat. Focus is on the FY capex guide and on whether Muse and ads monetization let management keep raising OPEX into 2027 without the stock being punished. Expectations are elevated, with META outperforming Mag 7 peers YTD on the Muse launch. Desk positioning is 8/10.

Credit was a major incremental development, worsened by rate hike concerns after last week's hotter than expected inflation print. AI-related HY spreads widened 25bp by midweek versus 2bp for non-AI issuers.
GIR forecasts $720bn of combined project finance and direct hyperscaler issuance in 2027. Investors are starting to question the cost of capital needed to sustain the investment cycle.
Neoclouds are a focal point, with the space down 25% last week. GIR upgraded CoreWeave to Buy (Gabriela Borges).

With AI capex growth potentially past its peak, credit quality, funding needs and ROIC are becoming more important to equity valuations. The earnings season tests whether strong fundamentals can stop the deterioration in sentiment and price momentum.

Early Q3 read (10% of S&P reported): 53% of firms beat consensus EPS by more than one standard deviation of analyst estimates. That is above the 25-year average of 50% but well below the 64% average of the past four quarters, which supports the view that earnings growth and estimate upgrades have peaked.
GIR US Strategy (Ben Snider) says the equity market has downgraded growth expectations on rising cost of capital. The Cyclicals vs. Defensives pair fell 6% over two weeks.

GS forecasts S&P 500 EPS growth of 36% in 2026, slowing to 11% in 2027, or 18% adjusted for non-recurring 2026 accounting distortions. AI capex contributes about half of S&P 500 EPS growth, and that impulse should fade as capex growth slows and depreciation builds.

GIR recommends secular growth over cyclicals in a slowing growth, narrow breadth backdrop. It suggests consumer-facing laggards for a catch-up and a screen of defensive quality stocks for a catch-down.

GS PB: Global Info Tech saw its largest de-grossing on record, driven by long selling in semis. US semis positioning is at the 39th percentile vs the past year and the 88th vs the past 5 years. 350 S&P stocks rose last week and SPX ex-AI outperformed by 475bp.

The HF VIP L/S pair (GSTHVIPP) fell 5.05% on the week, its worst week since Covid. Semis are down about 25% relative to the S&P from their highs, and 20+ years of SOX vs SPX drawdown history suggests the move may be near its limit.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong fundamentals and earnings confirmation could stop the deterioration in sentiment. Positioning is already low after a record de-grossing, semis are down about 25% relative to the S&P, and SOX vs SPX drawdown history suggests the move may be near its end.
tension_points.bear_case: AI capex growth may be past its peak. Rising cost of capital and wider AI-related HY spreads raise funding questions, and the rate of earnings growth and estimate upgrades appears to have peaked.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Earnings failing to confirm strong fundamentals this season, with META's FY capex guide and OPEX commentary the first test.
